answer_raw:
For the fastest performance, you should rent a **GPU Droplet** at **$2.50/hr** (as of 2026) [2]. 

Running a 7B model on a standard CPU-based Droplet is technically possible but will be painfully slow due to the compute requirements of LLM inference. If you want a functional experience for a 7B model, you'll want to look at the **Premium Intel (2 vCPU/4GB RAM)** option for **$24/mo** (as of 2026) [1], or ideally, move to the GPU-based instances.

The cheapest droplet available is the **Basic Droplet** at **$4/mo** (undated) [2][6]. However, with only **512 MiB of RAM** and **1 shared vCPU** (undated) [6], it will not be able to run a t-scale 7B model; it is intended for tiny hobbyist tasks and minimal web serving.

## Comparison of Options

| Option | Price | Best Use Case |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **GPU Droplet** | **$2.50/hr** (as of 2026) [2] | **Fastest** performance for LLM inference. |
| **Premium Intel Droplet** | **$24/mo** (as of 2026) [1] | A baseline for small, lightweight tasks. |
| **Basic Droplet** | **$4/mo** (undated) [2][6] | Minimalist tasks; will not run a 7B model. |

For a 7B model, you typically need significantly more than 512 MiB of RAM. Even with 4GB of RAM, you would likely need to use heavy quantization (like 4-bit) just to fit the model weights into memory, and even then, the CPU-only inference would be extremely slow. If you are looking for a production-ready environment, the **GPU Droplet** is the only clear choice for speed.
